questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I chose Australia because I wanted to study in an English-speaking country, which would help me improve my English skills. I also wanted to experience living in a country that is far away and not somewhere I would normally have the opportunity to visit again. That made Australia an exciting and unique study destination for me.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was fairly easy to find the information I needed upon arrival. The University of Copenhagen (KU) provided a lot of useful information before and during the exchange, which helped me get started. I was also fortunate to know other students who had already been on exchange, and they shared their experiences and practical advice, which made the transition much easier.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Monash University was very good at providing information and support when I arrived. They organized a well-structured orientation week, where we received practical information about the university, campus facilities, student life, and administrative procedures. The orientation made it easy to settle in, and the staff were helpful and available to answer any questions we had.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
It was a bit challenging to find off-campus housing. I used
Flatmates.com.au
to look for accommodation, but it was difficult because I wanted to see the properties in person before committing. This meant there was some uncertainty before I arrived. I stayed in an Airbnb during my first week, which gave me time to attend inspections. Fortunately, I was offered the very first room I viewed, but I know that finding housing can be quite competitive. On the positive side, many people move in and out throughout the semester, so new rooms become available regularly. I would recommend arriving a little early and arranging temporary accommodation while searching for a permanent place.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Future exchange students should know that finding off-campus housing can take some time, so it is a good idea to arrange temporary accommodation for the first few days or week. Although it can be challenging to find a place, I would definitely recommend living closer to the city rather than near Monash University. Living in the city gave me a much better social experience, with easy access to restaurants, cafés, events, and public transport, while it was still possible to commute to campus.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The registration process required us to choose our own courses and have them approved by both our home university and Monash University. After that, we had to build our own timetable by selecting classes that fit together without scheduling conflicts. I found this part a bit challenging, as it required some planning and flexibility. However, Monash University provided good support throughout the process, and the staff were very helpful whenever I had questions or needed assistance.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You could write to Monash.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Pretty successful. I ended up with all the classes I preferred.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: My advice would be to start the registration process as early as possible, as it can take some time to get your courses approved and create a timetable that works. Don't hesitate to ask for help if you are unsure about anything - the staff at Monash are very helpful and respond quickly to questions. I would also recommend watching the videos on the Monash website, as they provide clear, step-by-step guidance through the registration process.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Overall, I found the level of the courses to be manageable and well balanced. The academic standard was similar to what I am used to at my home university, and I felt that I could follow the lectures and assignments without major difficulties. Some courses were more demanding than others, but in general the workload was reasonable, and it was possible to keep up as long as I stayed consistent with the readings and coursework.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The main difference in teaching style compared to UCPH was that there was more focus on tutorials or smaller group classes, while lectures were often provided online rather than in person. Another significant difference was the assessment style. Instead of traditional exams, most of my courses were assessed through larger assignments and projects. This meant a more continuous workload throughout the semester compared to exam periods at UCPH.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Conflict, security and development, Gender and development, Foundations of international relations, Peacekeeping in the international system

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend conflict, security and development and Peacekeeping in the international system. Both courses was inspiring and the teacher was very professional.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Overall, I did not experience many unexpected costs during my stay. However, I did find that rent in Australia was quite expensive compared to what I am used to. In addition, the visa application for Australia was also quite costly. Apart from these two main expenses, there were no major surprises in terms of additional costs.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Rent was more expensive

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There were a wide variety of cultural, athletic, and social activities available for students at Monash University. Many different student clubs and societies organized events throughout the semester, ranging from cultural groups to sports and hobby-based clubs. I personally joined an outdoor club, which offered activities and trips that made it easy to meet new people and explore the surrounding nature. Overall, there were plenty of opportunities to get involved and be socially active outside of classes.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would definitely recommend going on road trips, as it is a great way to explore Australia and experience the country beyond the city. I would also encourage future exchange students to take advantage of the cultural opportunities available, especially in Melbourne. There are many interesting museums, galleries, and events, and a lot of them are quite affordable for students. Overall, combining travel with cultural activities makes the exchange experience much more rewarding.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: New Zealand!! Or Great Ocean Road

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy. Australia is an easy country to live in

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Go to your classes and do not skip them or take to many online classes

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I did not experience any major cultural differences that I found particularly challenging. Overall, I adapted quite easily to the environment, and I felt comfortable living and studying in Australia. Any differences I noticed were more interesting than difficult, and they did not significantly affect my daily life.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I especially appreciated how relaxed and easy-going the culture was. People were very approachable and welcoming, which made it easy to meet new people and feel comfortable in a new environment. There was a generally friendly and informal atmosphere in both academic and social settings, which I really enjoyed during my stay.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
First, even though the planning process can feel overwhelming at times - especially with course selection, housing, and registration - it is absolutely worth it in the end.

Second, I would recommend being proactive and not hesitating to ask for help. The university staff are generally very supportive, and there are many resources available if you are unsure about anything.

Third, make sure to take advantage of everything the exchange experience has to offer, both socially and culturally. There are many opportunities to meet new people, join clubs, travel, and explore, and these experiences are a big part of what makes the exchange so valuable.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The most rewarding part of my exchange experience was meeting new people, exploring different places, and having the opportunity to travel. It was very enriching to build friendships with people from different backgrounds and to experience Australia beyond the university setting. I also really enjoyed my courses, which I found interesting and engaging, and they contributed a lot to my overall experience.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Finding a place to live

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
